title: Archie Bleyer's correspondence course and band
summary: He takes Bleyer's course, plays in his band, and decides he is not a very good trumpet player.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: we've gotten as far as the Columbia Blue Lions.
Let me think. In 1930--this is two years before I went to Columbia--
When did you go to Columbia?

Yes; he also had a correspondence course and I took that and got to know him. In '31--I think it was '31, he started a band and I got to play in it, this was over in Westchester somewhere. Fletcher Henderson at that time had gone down the street--there were bands all over the Post Road in those days. I got to know Fletcher later in Benny's band. It kind of convinced me I was never a very good trumpet player. I had gotten kicked in the lip when
I was playing football in high school before that. I played a great low G. I did that in Red Norvo's band, still playing trumpet then.
Yeah, that was earlier; that was a freak.
